# Rankings and measurements

*Generated by `scripts/report.py`. Do not hand-edit.*

## Test bed

Measured inside Docker Linux containers (aarch64) on a 4 vCPU / 8 GB VM — chosen to approximate a small VPS. Servers and the benchmark client share that budget, as they would on a real single-box deployment.

## Correctness under contention (the discriminator)

8 writer processes, 4 hot keys, read-modify-write `+1`. Every engine was asked to do the same unsafe-looking thing; the question is what it does about it.

| engine | ops/s | p50 ms | p99 ms | error rate | correctness |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sqlite` | 26228.4 | 0.023 | 0.291 | 0.0% | CORRECT |
| `redis` | 16183.3 | 0.185 | 4.105 | 0.0% | CORRECT |
| `sqlite-naive` | 11288.8 | 0.03 | 1.512 | 58.5% | CORRECT |
| `redis-naive` | 7696.1 | 0.262 | 8.242 | 0.0% | **LOST UPDATES** (163 of 1600) |
| `postgres` | 3073.1 | 1.691 | 10.469 | 0.0% | CORRECT |
| `postgres-naive` | 2850.8 | 1.9 | 15.434 | 0.0% | **LOST UPDATES** (757 of 1600) |
| `qdrant` | 773.9 | 7.492 | 33.864 | 0.0% | **LOST UPDATES** (737 of 1600) |
| `duckdb` | 354.0 | 2.165 | 12.365 | 3.382% | CORRECT |
| `lancedb` | 94.4 | 26.149 | 612.188 | 0.0% | **LOST UPDATES** (822 of 1600) |

> Read the last two columns together. A high error rate with a `CORRECT` verdict means the engine **refused** work it could not do safely — that is the good failure. A 0% error rate next to `LOST UPDATES` means it accepted every write and silently discarded some.

*These runs were measured on the busy host, so the ops/s column is depressed by ~2-3x relative to the append table. The correctness column is unaffected — losing an update is not a performance characteristic.*

## Append throughput vs writer count

Agent event-stream appends, ops/s, on an otherwise-idle host. Median where a cell was measured more than once (`×n` marks how many observations). The *shape* of each row — flat, rising, or collapsing — is the finding; see measurement noise below for the error bar.

| engine | 1 writer | 4 writers | 8 writers | 16 writers | best p50 ms | max err |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sqlite` | 45,360 | 45,677 | 43,904 ×4 | 38,566 | 0.011 | 0.0% |
| `redis` | 8,965 | 25,731 | 44,202 ×4 | 42,049 | 0.101 | 0.0% |
| `postgres` | 4,734 | 10,220 | 14,770 ×4 | 18,184 | 0.177 | 0.0% |
| `sqlite-naive` | — | — | 7,659 | — | 0.043 | 98.376% |
| `duckdb` | 815 | 592 | 803 | 722 | 1.118 | 0.207% |
| `lancedb` | 322 | 125 | 61 | 53 | 2.873 | 0.0% |

### The same benchmark on a busy host

Part of the sweep ran while an unrelated container held ~177% CPU of 4 cores (and the Docker daemon crashed once under the load). Those runs are kept and labelled rather than discarded, because a cheap VPS is an oversubscribed, noisy-neighbour environment by definition — this is what that costs.

| engine | writers | busy host | idle host | penalty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `duckdb` | 1 | 447 | 815 | 1.8x |
| `duckdb` | 4 | 431 | 592 | 1.4x |
| `duckdb` | 8 | 682 | 803 | 1.2x |
| `lancedb` | 1 | 175 | 322 | 1.8x |
| `lancedb` | 4 | 59 | 125 | 2.1x |
| `lancedb` | 8 | 23 | 61 | 2.7x |
| `postgres` | 1 | 2,084 | 4,734 | 2.3x |
| `postgres` | 4 | 5,064 | 10,220 | 2.0x |
| `postgres` | 8 | 6,746 | 14,770 | 2.2x |
| `postgres` | 16 | 18,938 | 18,184 | 1.0x |
| `redis` | 1 | 5,475 | 8,965 | 1.6x |
| `redis` | 4 | 11,372 | 25,731 | 2.3x |
| `redis` | 8 | 19,130 | 44,202 | 2.3x |
| `redis` | 16 | 41,048 | 42,049 | 1.0x |
| `sqlite` | 1 | 32,129 | 45,360 | 1.4x |
| `sqlite` | 4 | 24,402 | 45,677 | 1.9x |
| `sqlite` | 8 | 18,839 | 43,904 | 2.3x |
| `sqlite` | 16 | 40,618 | 38,566 | 0.9x |

> Throughput fell by roughly 2-3x across the board, and **the ranking did not change**. Contention scales everything down together; it does not reorder the engines. Absolute ops/s on a shared VPS should be discounted accordingly.

## Vector recall

30,000 vectors x 384 dimensions, top-10, cosine, single-threaded. Data is **clustered** (300 centers), because 384-dimensional uniform random vectors are all nearly equidistant — against uniform data every ANN index scores near-zero recall, which measures the generator rather than the engine. Recall is against exact cosine on the same data.

| engine | index | load | index build | p50 ms | qps | recall@1 | recall@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `redis` | hnsw (vector set, default) | 34.17 s | 0.0 s | 1.458 | 619.4 | 70.5% | 33.7% |
| `postgres (ef=40)` | hnsw(m=16,ef_c=64,ef_s=40) | 3.92 s | 12.09 s | 1.507 | 626.0 | 43.0% | 19.4% |
| `qdrant` | hnsw(m=16, default) | 6.78 s | 0.0 s | 3.437 | 243.4 | 98.5% | 80.1% |
| `lancedb` | ivf_pq(64,48) | 0.66 s | 31.15 s | 5.618 | 152.5 | 73.0% | 22.95% |
| `postgres (ef=400)` | hnsw(m=16,ef_c=64,ef_s=400) | 2.86 s | 10.3 s | 7.752 | 127.9 | 96.5% | 71.85% |
| `postgres (exact)` | seqscan (no index, exact) | 2.89 s | 0.0 s | 15.001 | 62.1 | 100.0% | 100.0% |
| `sqlite` | brute-force | 0.86 s | 0.0 s | 18.98 | 50.6 | 100.0% | 100.0% |

> `recall@1` — did it find the single true nearest neighbour — is the number that matters for agent recall, where one strongly-matching memory is usually the point. `recall@10` punishes an index for reordering near-ties that are all equally good answers.

## Hard filters

**46 options considered → 16 survive → 30 eliminated.**

Eliminated options are not bad options; they fail a requirement that no amount of speed compensates for.

| option | why it is out |
|---|---|
| Flat markdown + JSONL (status quo) | fails multi_process_write — mpw: no atomic read-modify-write across processes; two agents updating one note is last-writer-wins |
| SQLite BEGIN CONCURRENT (wal2 branch) | fails maintained — mnt: an unmerged experimental branch of SQLite; shipping it means maintaining a custom build indefinitely |
| SQLite HC-tree backend | fails maintained — mnt: experimental, no stable on-disk format, no release date |
| DuckDB (+ VSS) | fails multi_process_write — mpw: MEASURED — 7 of 8 writer processes could not open the database file at all (rmw workload, connect errors); only one p |
| PGlite (Postgres compiled to WASM) | fails multi_process_write — mpw: single process, single connection by design |
| Kùzu (embedded property graph) | fails multi_process_write, maintained — mnt: acquired by Apple Oct 2025, repository archived. mpw: single writer |
| CozoDB (Datalog + vector + graph, embedded) | fails maintained — mnt: development dormant |
| redb / sled / fjall / RocksDB (+ usearch) | fails multi_process_write — mpw: redb/sled/fjall allow one process to hold the file read-write; RocksDB likewise |
| LanceDB (Lance columnar format) | fails multi_process_write — mpw: MEASURED — 822 of 1600 read-modify-write updates lost at 8 writers, with zero errors reported. No atomic update primi |
| Chroma | fails multi_process_write, store_of_record — mpw: embedded mode is single-process. sor: a vector index, not a state store |
| Milvus Lite / Milvus standalone | fails multi_process_write, fits_small_vps, store_of_record — fit: standalone needs etcd + object storage, ~500 MB idle. mpw: Lite is single-process |
| FAISS / hnswlib / usearch / Annoy | fails multi_process_write, store_of_record — sor: an index in RAM with no durability or concurrency; it is a component of a database, not one |
| Qdrant | fails store_of_record — sor: MEASURED — no transactional primitive; set_payload read-modify-write loses updates. Excellent as a retrieval index beside |
| Weaviate | fails store_of_record — sor: no cross-object transactions |
| Typesense / Meilisearch | fails store_of_record — sor: a search index, explicitly not a system of record |
| Elasticsearch / OpenSearch | fails fits_small_vps, store_of_record — fit: ~1.2 GB idle JVM. sor: near-real-time refresh breaks read-your-own-write |
| ClickHouse | fails store_of_record — sor: no transactions and no efficient row updates; mutable agent state is the wrong shape for it |
| TiDB / CockroachDB / YugabyteDB | fails fits_small_vps — fit: a Raft cluster needs ~2 GB before it does anything useful |
| NATS JetStream (streams + KV) | fails store_of_record — sor: no query capability at all — you cannot ask it a question about the data it holds |
| Kafka / Redpanda | fails fits_small_vps, store_of_record — fit: ~500 MB idle. sor: a log, not a queryable store |
| Neo4j / Memgraph / FalkorDB | fails fits_small_vps — fit: ~700 MB idle for Neo4j; FalkorDB is lighter but still a second daemon for a few thousand notes |
| XTDB / Datomic (bitemporal, immutable) | fails fits_small_vps — fit: ~600 MB JVM |
| ElectricSQL / Zero / PowerSync | fails store_of_record — sor: a replication layer over Postgres — it presupposes the answer rather than being one |
| Automerge / Yjs (CRDTs) | fails store_of_record — sor: converges without choosing a winner, so task claims and counters are structurally unrepresentable |
| FoundationDB | fails fits_small_vps, store_of_record — fit: cluster overhead. sor: a substrate you build a database on, with a 5-second transaction limit |
| Managed Postgres (RDS / Aurora / Neon / Supabase / Timescale) | fails self_hostable — shs: writes require the network; violates the charter rule that every dependency is a local process or file |
| Turso Cloud (managed libSQL) | fails self_hostable — shs: writes go to the cloud authority |
| Mem0 | fails store_of_record — sor: a policy layer that still requires you to choose the database underneath it |
| Zep / Graphiti (temporal knowledge graph) | fails store_of_record — sor: same — a memory framework over a backing store, and its preferred backend (Kuzu) is archived |
| Letta (MemGPT) | fails store_of_record — sor: owns the agent loop, which collides with Jod's 'harnesses think, Jod delegates' rule |

> **Top-3 stability** is how often an option stays in the top three across 2,000 runs with the weights jittered by ±1 and every *judged* (not measured) score jittered by ±0.5. A high score with low stability means the ranking, not the option, is doing the work.
